Question: Mitchell is trying to chew his way through a deck of 32 playing cards. He starts by chewing on 4 cards, then eats twice as many cards as he ate on the previous round. How many more cards does Mitchell need to chew to finish the deck?
Assistant:
<think>
Mitchell eats 4 cards in the first round.
In the second round, he eats twice as many as the first round, so 4 cards x 2 = 8 cards.
At the end of the second round, Mitchell has eaten 4 cards + 8 cards = 12 cards.
There are 32 cards in total, and Mitchell has done 12 cards, so 32 - 12 = 20 cards remaining.
Mitchell needs to eat 20 more rounds to chew through the remaining 20 cards.
In each round, he has two-thirds of the cards he eats on the third round, so he eats 4 cards x (2/3) = 8 cards in the third round.
After the third round, there will be 32 - 20 = 12 cards remaining.
Mitchell needs to eat 12 cards in the fourth round.
In the fourth round, he eats 4 cards x (2/3) x (2/3) = 16/9 ≈ 1.78 cards, so he can eat 2 cards to chew the last two cards (since he can only eat whole cards).
However, since he needs to chew all 20 cards in total, he also needs to chew three more cards in order to finish the rest.
Therefore, Mitchell needs to eat 12 + 3 = 15 more cards to finish the deck.
<answer> 15 cards </answer>
